text:
Predicates:
Win(x) ::: x always wins.
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
Lose(x) ::: x loses.
Conclusion:
Lose(nemesis) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → Win(x)) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x (GoodGuy(x) ↔ Fight(x, badGuys)) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ((SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, character(y))) → GoodGuy(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y ((Win(x) ∧ Fight(x, y)) → Lose(y)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
∀x ((SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, character(y))) → Character(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
